title: SOC2 probing notebook — initial control hypotheses
content:
Purpose: rough, personal scratchpad for early SOC 2 prep. Not a final mapping — quick hypotheses, places to look for evidence, and questions to bring to the control owners. Keep messy; will convert to a formal spreadsheet once owners confirmed.

Top-level framing (one-liner): Redwood Inference needs a minimal defendable evidence set for Security + Availability (TSC) for hosted & dedicated products; private deployments will need additional customer-specific evidence. Focus first on canned/hosted API flows where we control the plane.

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- Start with access control, change control, incident mgmt, config mgmt (these are low-friction).
- Hosted API likely has best centralized evidence: access logs, IAM roles, onboarding docs, incident runbooks.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity: evidence might be split (billing/contractual + infra snapshots).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): need customer attestations + deployment runbooks + KMS evidence.

Quick control hypotheses (map to Trust Services Criteria buckets):
1) Logical access (Security): IAM role lists + onboarding/offboarding ticket links + Okta group membership exports. Owner candidate: People Ops + Platform IAM. Evidence to pull: Okta reports (last 90d), GCP service account usage reports, RBAC doc.
2) Change control (Processing Integrity / Security): GitHub PR workflow, code review policy, release notes. Owner: Release Engineering. Evidence: PR history for last 3 releases, CI pipeline config, deployment approvals.
3) Monitoring & alerting (Availability): SRE runbooks, PagerDuty rotations, alert thresholds, on-call calendar. Owner: SRE. Evidence: PagerDuty slogs, alert history, postmortems.
4) Data encryption (Confidentiality): KMS integration notes, envelope encryption design, key rotation schedule. Owners: Infra Eng + Security. Evidence: KMS audit logs, config in Terraform, rotation tickets.
5) Vendor/subservice management (Security/Availability): contracts with cloud provider, subprocessors list. Owner: Legal / Procurement. Evidence: contracts, subprocessors spreadsheet.

Evidence locations (initial guesses):
- Okta: admin report exports (ask Katya or Noam to run)
- GCP Audit Logs: project:redwood-inference-prod, BigQuery exports bucket
- GitHub: org -> repo -> protected branch merge history (release-engineering)
- PagerDuty: service 'redwood-core' -> incidents -> oncall schedules
- Confluence: SOC2 checklist (starter) -> will link later

Open questions (to resolve in triage):
1) How do we prove access removal for contractors who used ephemeral GitHub access? (ask People Ops)
2) For Dedicated customers, do we consider the dedicated pool as 'shared' infra for SOC2 scope, or treat only the control plane (console/API) as in-scope? (product + legal)
3) Private deployments: do we accept customer-hosted audit logs as evidence, or require a vendor-signed checklist? (compliance)
4) Do we have automated S3 bucket scanning for public exposures? If not, add as compensating control. (infra)

Sketch of a control mapping (very rough) — will move to sheet:
- CC: Logical access -> Control: Okta groups + GitHub org membership + IAM role reviews -> Evidence: group export, monthly review tickets, IAM change logs -> Owner: People Ops / Platform IAM
- CC: Change control -> Control: PR-based merges, release approvals, deployment gating -> Evidence: GitHub PRs, CHANGELOG, CI logs -> Owner: Release Engineering
- CC: Incident response -> Control: oncall rota + incident runbooks + postmortems -> Evidence: PagerDuty incidents, postmortem docs -> Owner: SRE

Short-term action list (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Ask Katya for Okta group exports (owner: me, due: 2024-03-15)
- [ ] Request GitHub protected branch merge history (owner: Isaac, due: 2024-03-16)
- [ ] Pull a sample GCP audit log slice and see retention (owner: Noah, due: 2024-03-18)
- [ ] Sync with Release Eng on an artefact list they can hand auditors (owner: Maya, due: 2024-03-20)

Interview prompts (for control owners) — quick bullets to ask in syncs:
- What is your designated control owner title and backup?
- Where is the evidence stored (link + retention)? Is it immutable?
- When was the control last exercised/tested? Any gaps?
- For manual steps: is there a ticketed trail? Who signs off?
- Any exceptions or legacy processes that auditors should know about?

Potential red flags (call out early):
- Lots of manual SSH key sharing (ask infra)
- No documented key rotation for service account keys older than 1y
- Paging only to personal phones without backup escalation

Notes on Private deployments (special):
- Need templated evidence pack we can hand customers: deployment checklist (network, KMS config, audit endpoint), minimal runbook for incident reporting, instructions for audit log export.
- Consider templated 'customer attestation' doc for controls they own.

Conversion plan: after owners identified, create a canonical spreadsheet with fields: Control ID, TSC pillar, Control description, Owner, Evidence list (link + sample), Frequency, Status, Risk rating, Notes. We'll keep a read-only copy in Confluence for auditors.

Random small reminders:
- Put all audit-related Slack convos in private channel and tag JIRA tasks to avoid scattering evidence.
- Keep snapshots (export) of evidence rather than live links where possible.

End-of-note: this is intentionally rough. Next step: schedule 30m with People Ops and Release Eng to validate the first 6 controls.

Signature: Isaac — rough SOC2 brain dump, 2024-03-12 10:23am
